questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the intercostal nerve a branch of?

options.text: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Ventral rami of thoracic spinal nerves
Ventral rami of cervical spinal nerves

questions.correctAnswerText: Ventral rami of thoracic spinal nerves
questions.explanation: The intercostal nerve is a branch of the ventral (anterior) ramus of a thoracic spinal nerve. The source notes that intercostal nerves are distributed primarily to the thoracic and abdominal walls: the first thoracic nerve contributes variably to the second nerve and passes into the brachial plexus; T3-T6 supply only the thoracic wall; T7-T11 supply both thoracic and abdominal walls; and the subcostal nerve supplies the abdominal wall and gluteal skin. Lateral and anterior cutaneous branches innervate the anterior chest wall, and the source identifies T6 with the xiphoid process.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The given image shows the posterior thoracic wall. Which of the following statements is false about the structure marked A within the intercostal space?

options.text: It is located below the intercostal artery
Derivatives from T4 and T5 are typical in type
They lie between external intercostal and internal intercostal muscle
Derivatives from T7 to T11 supply the abdominal wall

questions.correctAnswerText: They lie between external intercostal and internal intercostal muscle
questions.explanation: The marked structure is the intercostal nerve. The false statement is that intercostal nerves lie between the external and internal intercostal muscles; the source places them between the internal and innermost intercostal muscles. Typical intercostal nerves supply only the thoracic wall, with the source describing T3-T6 as typical; upper intercostal nerves have special distributions, T2 gives the intercostobrachial nerve, and T7-T11 continue to the abdominal wall as thoracoabdominal nerves. In each intercostal space the main neurovascular bundle is arranged superior-to-inferior as vein, artery, nerve (VAN), with a collateral SVAN bundle.

questions.question: A patient who underwent right-sided mastectomy is now complaining of pain over the axilla and medial aspect of the right upper arm. What is the nerve involved a branch of?

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient diagnosed with empyema was planned for intercostal drainage tube insertion. During the procedure, which of the following muscles is not pierced?
questions.explanation: Intercostal drainage tubes are placed in the mid-axillary line, and transversus thoracis is not pierced because it lies anteriorly rather than in the mid-axillary line. The source also calls transversus thoracis triangularis sternae or sternocostalis, gives its origin from the lower third of the posterior surface of the sternum, xiphoid process and lower 3-4 rib cartilages, and its insertion into cartilages of the second to sixth ribs. The innermost muscle plane includes innermost intercostals laterally, subcostals posteriorly and transversus thoracis anteriorly.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the left phrenic nerve?

options.text: Arise from dorsal rami of C2, C3, and C4
Descends in the left pleural space
Supplies the parietal peritoneum on the diaphragm
Passes through the vena caval opening in the diaphragm

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies the parietal peritoneum on the diaphragm
questions.explanation: The left phrenic nerve supplies sensory fibers to the parietal peritoneum covering the diaphragm. The source states that it is a mixed nerve derived mainly from C4 with contributions from C3 and C5 ventral rami, formed at the lateral border of scalenus anterior. It descends anterior to the pulmonary hilum between mediastinal pleura and fibrous pericardium, passes through the muscular diaphragm just anterior to the central tendon, and supplies motor fibers to the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm plus sensory fibers to mediastinal pleura, fibrous/serous pericardium and diaphragmatic peritoneum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 50-year-old woman presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and weight loss. Chest X-ray showed an elevated right dome of the diaphragm. CT revealed a tumor invading the right lung surface anterior to the hilum. Which of the following nerves is most likely to be involved by the tumor?
questions.explanation: The right phrenic nerve is most likely involved because it passes anterior to the lung hilum. The phrenic nerve provides the sole motor supply to the diaphragm; paralysis causes the respective dome to flatten when intact or move paradoxically on inspiration. The source contrasts the vagus nerve, which passes posterior to the hilum, and notes that recurrent laryngeal nerves are not related to the lung surface in this way.

questions.question: A fluoroscopic examination is being performed in a patient with suspected phrenic nerve palsy. On asking the patient to inspire, you observe the following in the diaphragm. Which of the following statements is correct about the course of the nerve involved?

options.text: It runs anterior to scalenus anterior
It lies posterior to brachial plexus
It lies posterior to subclavian artery
It runs behind the left hilum

questions.correctAnswerText: It runs anterior to scalenus anterior
questions.explanation: The source identifies left phrenic palsy from paradoxical elevation of the left dome and states that the left phrenic nerve runs anterior to scalenus anterior. In the cervical region both phrenic nerves pass anterior to scalenus anterior and posterior to sternocleidomastoid/inferior belly of omohyoid. The left phrenic nerve is posterior to internal jugular vein, transverse cervical artery and suprascapular artery, and posterior to the thoracic duct on the left. At the root of the neck it runs medial to the brachial plexus, anterior to the second part of the subclavian artery and posterior to the subclavian vein. In the thorax it descends anterior to the pulmonary hilum.

questions.question: Rib notching was observed on chest X-ray in a patient with Turner's syndrome due to enlargement of arteries in the inferior rib margin. Which of the following is incorrect about these arteries?

options.text: They supply the intercostal space up to the costo-chondral junction
First two pairs arise from branches of the thyrocervical trunk
Arteries on the right are longer than the corresponding ones on the left
There are 11 pairs of posterior intercostal arteries

questions.explanation: Rib notching is produced by enlarged posterior intercostal arteries, classically in coarctation of the aorta. The source states that there are 11 pairs and notes that they supply the intercostal spaces to the costochondral junction.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: In a patient with inferior vena caval obstruction, which of the following collaterals do not help drain the blood?

options.text: Superior epigastric and inferior epigastric vein

questions.explanation: The source states that superficial epigastric and iliolumbar veins do not help bypass inferior vena cava obstruction: the iliolumbar vein drains directly into the IVC and the superficial epigastric vein drains through the femoral system. In IVC obstruction, collateral routes use azygos/hemiazygos veins and vertebral venous plexuses; communications also involve iliac channels and tributaries of the IVC, inferior/superior epigastric veins, internal thoracic veins, brachiocephalic veins and the superior vena cava.

structuredExplanation.text: The source states that superficial epigastric and iliolumbar veins do not help bypass inferior vena cava obstruction: the iliolumbar vein drains directly into the IVC and the superficial epigastric vein drains through the femoral system. In IVC obstruction, collateral routes use azygos/hemiazygos veins and vertebral venous plexuses; communications also involve iliac channels and tributaries of the IVC, inferior/superior epigastric veins, internal thoracic veins, brachiocephalic veins and the superior vena cava.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 2-year-old girl playing with small magnets suddenly develops breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows an inhaled foreign body in one of the bronchi. Where does the vein supplying the most likely site of obstruction drain into?
questions.explanation: An inhaled foreign body most commonly enters the right bronchus because the right principal bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical. The source states that right bronchial veins drain into the azygos vein, whereas left bronchial veins drain into accessory hemiazygos or the left superior intercostal vein.
